name: Cervicogenic Headache
definition: Headache attributed to a disorder of the cervical spine and its structures, typically accompanied by neck pain and restricted or provocative cervical movement. Other primary and secondary headache disorders must be excluded.

typical: Unilateral or side-dominant headache associated with neck pain
Headache provoked by neck movement or sustained posture

redFlags.item: Acute visual loss or temporal arteritis features

core: Blood pressure and cranial/neurological assessment when indicated

investigations.principle: Routine cervical imaging is not required for typical uncomplicated cases.
investigations.MRI: MRI/vascular or brain imaging is selected when red flags or alternative pathology is suspected.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs have limited value for diagnosing the pain source.

green: Education, posture/activity modification and cervical/scapular exercise
Manual therapy only when serious vascular/neurological disease is excluded
amber: High-velocity cervical manipulation requires careful risk assessment and is inappropriate when vascular or neurological red flags exist.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Shirah-shoola with cervical contribution may be documented descriptively; modern headache differential remains essential.

patientEducation.summary: Headache attributed to a disorder of the cervical spine and its structures, typically accompanied by neck pain and restricted or provocative cervical movement. Other primary and secondary headache disorders must be excluded.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
